title: The Essential Strategy of Repurposing an Existing Product or Resource
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This short piece makes the case for repurposing existing products, content, and resources before chasing new ones. Borrowing the restaurant concept of 'ingredient stretching,' it argues that finding new audiences or uses for proven work is often more efficient and profitable than building something new from scratch. It notes this strategy is frequently overlooked because it feels less exciting than launching something novel. The conclusion urges leaders to look hard at what they've already built before investing in the next new thing.
points: Repurposing proven content or products for new audiences is often more efficient than building something new.
The restaurant-world concept of 'ingredient stretching' is offered as the guiding metaphor.
Repurposing strategies are frequently overlooked because they feel less exciting than new development.
Team members often enjoy seeing their existing work reach a wider audience.
Leaders are urged to fully capitalize on what already exists before chasing disruption.
quotes: Before investing in the development of new offerings, savvy leaders do their best to get even more out of what they have already generated.
In the restaurant world, chefs call this strategic expansion “ingredient stretching.
Repurposing or expanding the audience with existing content, products or materials usually requires fewer resources and investment.
Gaining more leverage from existing materials is often overlooked.
Good leaders don’t recycle. They find new and better ways to benefit from what they have already developed.
